The sky appears blue because of a phenomenon called **Rayleigh scattering**. Sunlight contains all colors of the visible spectrum, but when it enters Earth's atmosphere, it collides with gas molecules (mostly nitrogen and oxygen). These molecules scatter shorter wavelengths of light—blue and violet—much more strongly than longer wavelengths like red and yellow.

Our eyes are more sensitive to blue than violet, and some violet light is absorbed by the upper atmosphere, so we perceive the sky as blue. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight passes through more atmosphere, scattering away most of the blue and leaving the longer red and orange wavelengths, which is why the sky takes on those colors then.
